harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to serve DHCP on lan-a (eth2, the discovered link to node3) handing out 10.10.1.100-200/24 with itself (10.10.1.1) as default router, and node2 (OPNsense) to serve DHCP on lan-b (vtnet2, the discovered link to node4) handing out 10.10.2.100-200/24 with itself (10.10.2.1) as default router. node3 and node4's second NICs were switched from unconfigured/static to NetworkManager DHCP-client profiles and now obtain address plus default route dynamically from their respective router. All four nodes were then restarted one at a time; each showed a changed boot identity and fully recovered DHCP service/lease state and connectivity afterward.
actions_performed: Mapped physical topology via arping: node1 eth2 <-> node3 enp8s0 (lan-a); node2 vtnet2 <-> node4 enp8s0 (lan-b); node1 eth1 <-> node2 vtnet1 is an unrelated router-to-router link and was left untouched

VyOS node1: set eth2 address 10.10.1.1/24; configured Kea-backed 'service dhcp-server' shared-network LANA, subnet 10.10.1.0/24 with subnet-id 1, default-router option 10.10.1.1, range 10.10.1.100-200, listen-interface eth2; committed and saved

OPNsense node2: added interface opt1=vtnet2 (static 10.10.2.1/24) and a firewall pass rule directly to config.xml; configured the OPNsense/Kea/dhcp4 model (general.enabled=1, interfaces=opt1, subnet4 10.10.2.0/24 with router option 10.10.2.1 and pool 10.10.2.100-200); applied via configctl interface reconfigure, configctl filter reload, and plugins_configure('kea_sync') plus template reload to regenerate kea-dhcp4.conf/keactrl.conf

Diagnosed and fixed a UDP/67 bind conflict: OPNsense's pre-existing baseline dnsmasq DHCP+DNS service (bound to vtnet0/lan, a non-functional legacy sample config for an unrelated subnet) was wildcard-binding port 67 and blocking Kea from binding on vtnet2; disabled dnsmasq persistently via config.xml (enable=0) and rc.conf.d so Kea could bind exclusively to 10.10.2.1:67
Started/verified kea-dhcp4 running on both node1 and node2

node3: bound the existing unused 'Wired connection 2' NetworkManager profile to enp8s0 with ipv4.method=auto, ipv6.method=disabled, autoconnect=yes; brought it up and confirmed lease 10.10.1.100 with default route via 10.10.1.1
node4: same NetworkManager DHCP-client configuration on enp8s0; confirmed lease 10.10.2.100 with default route via 10.10.2.1
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id/kern.boottime, interface/DHCP/lease state) on all 4 nodes
Restarted node1 (VyOS 'reboot'), polled until exec was available again, confirmed new boot_id and that eth2 address, Kea process, and DHCP lease file all persisted

Restarted node2 (OPNsense '/sbin/reboot'), polled until exec was available again, confirmed new kern.boottime, that vtnet2 address, Kea process (bound cleanly to 10.10.2.1:67 with dnsmasq correctly staying disabled), and the DHCP lease all persisted
Restarted node3 (RHEL10 'reboot'), polled until exec was available again, confirmed new boot_id and that NetworkManager auto-reacquired the same DHCP lease/default route from node1
Restarted node4 (RHEL10 'reboot'), polled until exec was available again, confirmed new boot_id and that NetworkManager auto-reacquired the same DHCP lease/default route from node2
Verified end-to-end reachability (ping) from each host to its router both before and after all restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) serves DHCP addresses from its own pool on lan-a to node3, handing itself out as default gateway
evidence.summary: VyOS DHCP config committed on eth2 (10.10.1.1/24); node3's NetworkManager DHCP client obtained 10.10.1.100/24 with default route via 10.10.1.1; lease file on node1 confirms node3's assignment

evidence.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) serves DHCP addresses from its own pool on lan-b to node4, handing itself out as default gateway
evidence.summary: OPNsense opt1/vtnet2 configured with static 10.10.2.1/24, Kea DHCPv4 config generated and service started; node4's NetworkManager DHCP client obtained 10.10.2.100/24 with default route via 10.10.2.1; lease file on node2 confirms node4's assignment

evidence.requirement: Root-caused and resolved DHCP failure on lan-b (port 67 bind conflict from baseline dnsmasq service)
evidence.summary: Kea logs showed DHCPSRV_OPEN_SOCKET_FAIL address-in-use; identified dnsmasq wildcard-bound to :67; disabled dnsmasq in config.xml/rc.conf.d; confirmed kea-dhcp4 then bound exclusively to 10.10.2.1:67

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e636d872...; reboot command acknowledged and returned before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id changed to 3488a1db...; eth2 address, Kea process, and lease file all confirmed intact; node3 ping to gateway succeeded

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 05:08:17; reboot acknowledged, SSH transport dropped as expected; post-reboot kern.boottime changed to 05:27:36; vtnet2 address, Kea process bound to 10.10.2.1:67, and lease all confirmed intact; node4 ping to gateway succeeded

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id b17495e3...; reboot acknowledged, connection reset confirming shutdown; post-reboot boot_id changed to 7295357f...; enp8s0 DHCP lease/route and gateway ping all confirmed recovered automatically via NetworkManager

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 19062a82...; reboot acknowledged, connection timeout confirming shutdown; post-reboot boot_id changed to 1ef6907f...; enp8s0 DHCP lease/route and gateway ping all confirmed recovered automatically via NetworkManager
